name: Dot-com bubble
mainTrigger: Rapid repricing of internet-related equities as public-market participation and IPO activity expanded.
mainCause: Expectations for internet-era growth ran materially ahead of proven earnings and viable business models.
historicalSummary: The NASDAQ Composite peaked at 5,048.62 on 10 March 2000 and reached 1,114.11 on 9 October 2002. The library uses those published benchmark observations; it does not infer a single aggregate capital-inflow figure.
keyLessons: A compelling technology can be economically transformative while many contemporaneous valuations remain unsustainable.
Narrative strength and capital access should be evaluated separately from revenue durability and unit economics.

timeline.title: Commercial internet acceleration
timeline.detail: The reference period begins; this is a historical framing date, not a claim of a single start point.

timeline.title: NASDAQ peak
timeline.detail: NASDAQ Composite closed at 5,048.62 on 10 March 2000.

timeline.title: Peak reclaimed
timeline.detail: The benchmark later exceeded its March 2000 closing high.

chart.method: Published NASDAQ Composite observations normalized to the March 2000 peak = 100. This is a comparison index only; it is not market capitalization or a capital-flow estimate.
